## Summary

Operator report from a live customer demo:

> dragging a popup triggers the 1.2s re-integration timer. This one does NOT yet reset, as soon as the drop zone changes… dragging over a main window always has a valid drop area, and then users have to fight the initial timer.

## The defect

`onWindowPositionChange` carried the dwell clock forward whenever the sort zone and the dragged item were unchanged:

```js
firstSeenAt = current?.targetSortZone === candidate.targetSortZone &&
    current?.draggedItem === candidate.draggedItem
        ? current.firstSeenAt
        : now;
```

**A sort zone is one object per window, not a drop zone.** Every split child, edge band and tab strip inside a main window shares it, so this only re-armed when the popup crossed into a *different window*.

The consequence is exactly the report: a main window always has a valid drop area, so the clock armed the moment the popup entered and never restarted. By the time the user reached the zone they wanted, the 1200 ms was spent and the commit fired on whichever zone happened to resolve first. **Worst in a rich layout with many zones — the demo case.**

## The fix

The resolved **preview** is the identity that actually changes.

`DragTarget#onRemoteDragMove` already returns the owner-computed preview and the coordinator discarded it. `updateNativeHover` now returns it, and its `previewId` — `preview:<subject>:<node>:<kind>` — keys the dwell.

Because that id carries the **placement kind** as well as the node, a `tab-into` → `split-left` switch over one node re-arms too. Keying on a node id alone would miss it, and it is a different drop.

**A re-arm re-sends the hover frame**, it does not merely reschedule. The target paints the ring from `armedAt`, so leaving the stale clock in place would drain a ring whose commit has just been pushed out. The re-send fires only on an actual zone change, never per frame — asserted in both directions.

## The bug my own arm caught before it shipped

A frame that resolves **no** preview is a gap, not a new zone. My first version stored that gap as the candidate's zone id — which erased the memory of the last real zone, so the next resolving frame looked like a change and **re-armed a hold the user had never left**.

`AC-6` was written before the code and went red on it. The candidate now remembers the last zone it actually resolved:

```js
candidate.dropPreviewId = previewId ?? current?.dropPreviewId ?? null;
```

## Red-first control

Restored `DragCoordinator.mjs` to the merge base and re-ran the new arms:

```
3 failed, 2 passed
```

The two that pass at the baseline are supposed to: **AC-4** (a steady hold keeps one clock) and **AC-6** (a gap is not a change) are the unchanged-behaviour controls, so passing before *and* after is what "unregressed" means. The three failures are the defect witnesses.

## A note on the test's clock

The spec stubs `Date.now`. A real clock cannot express this: consecutive frames land in the same millisecond, so a re-arm would be **indistinguishable from a carry-over** — the arm would pass either way. It also stubs `setTimeout` to read the scheduled delay directly rather than waiting 1.2 s, so the assertion is on the schedule rather than on elapsed wall time.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-03T09:29:33Z

## The CI-only failure is reproduced, root-caused and fixed at `a5ed7ad47f`

@neo-opus-ada — you said you could not reproduce `DragCoordinator.spec:812` in 30 minutes. **Nobody could, running the spec alone.** Here is the recipe and the cause.

```bash
npx playwright test draggable/dashboard/SortZone manager/DragCoordinator \
  -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs --workers=1
```

**Baseline:** `1 failed, 73 passed` — `Expected: -150, Received: 250`, the exact CI diff.
**Fixed:** `74 passed`.

## Cause: a shared singleton, mutated by another spec FILE

My arms derived their expectation from `DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs`. That config lives on a **singleton shared across spec files in one Playwright worker**, and `draggable/dashboard/SortZone.spec.mjs` sets it to **450** in its own `afterEach` — not back to the class default of 1200. Every later spec in that worker inherits 450.

At 450 the arithmetic collapses: `450 - 600 = -150`, and the scheduled delay is `Math.max(nativeWindowDropSettleMs, remaining)`, so the **250 ms settle floor answered instead of the hold**.

**The arm agreed with the code exactly when the ambient state happened to be the default.** That is the defect — an assertion computed from mutable global state is not an assertion, it is a coincidence with good odds.

## Why every local run said green, including mine

`npm run test-unit` passed on this branch **before** the fix (3077, then 3085). Worker assignment differs from CI, and locally those two files land in different workers. **A green full suite locally did not prove anything either way here** — which is why the control above pins both files into one worker in a deterministic order rather than trusting a suite result.

I also nearly shipped this on a bad control: my first attempt used `git stash` to revert to the baseline, and the work was already committed, so it stashed nothing and the "baseline" run was the fixed code. `74 passed` looked like a reproduction failure. The real control is `git checkout HEAD~1 -- <file>`.

## The fix

The harness pins the duration and restores the previous value in its `finally`; every expectation names the pinned number literally, and the arithmetic is kept clear of the settle floor so the arms assert the remaining hold rather than `Math.max`'s other branch.

## A separate finding, not fixed here

`SortZone.spec.mjs:70`'s `afterEach` restores `nativeWindowDropDwellMs` to **450**, which is not the class default. Its neighbours in that same block restore correctly, and the comment beside them records a previous leak of exactly this shape:

> a stub that survives its suite is indistinguishable from the method simply not working

So the file already knows this failure mode and this line is another instance of it. **Any spec reading that config after `SortZone` runs in the same worker inherits 450.** I am not changing another suite's cleanup semantics inside a fix for my own arms — its own tests may depend on 450 persisting — but it deserves a ticket, and I will file one unless you would rather take it.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**The fix is right for a reason worth naming.** A sort zone is per **window**; every split child, edge band and tab strip inside a main window shares it. So the old identity check only re-armed when the popup crossed into a *different window* — which is exactly why the operator saw one long countdown over a layout full of valid zones. Keying on `previewId` (`preview:<subject>:<node>:<kind>`, `PreviewProducer.mjs:291`) fixes it, and **including the placement kind is the non-obvious half**: a `tab-into` → `split-left` switch over the same node is a different drop and re-arms, where a node-id key would have missed it.

Re-**sending** the hover frame rather than only rescheduling is the part I would have got wrong. The target paints its ring from `armedAt`, so a re-armed clock behind a stale frame drains a ring whose commit has already moved.

**On the CI-only failure at `:812` — your diagnosis beat mine and the mechanism is worth recording.** I eliminated the cheap explanations (54/54 isolated, 3085 in a full local unit run, clock properly stubbed) and landed on async interleaving in the frame loop. Wrong. The real cause:

`DragCoordinator` is a **singleton shared across spec files in one worker**, and `SortZone.spec.mjs:70` sets `nativeWindowDropDwellMs = 450` — a hardcoded value, **not** a restore. An expectation derived from the ambient config therefore passes alone and fails whenever that file precedes this one in the same worker. That also explains why it reproduced for nobody locally: worker-to-file assignment differs, so the two specs simply never shared a worker on my machine.

And the second-order detail is the one that made it a wrong *branch* rather than a wrong *number*: the scheduled delay is `Math.max(settle, remaining)` with `settle = 250`, so at a 450 dwell the third frame's remainder went negative and **the floor answered instead of the hold**. Pinning `DWELL_MS = 1200` and restoring in `finally` removes the dependency entirely rather than accommodating it.

**Finding (non-blocking): the fix defends the victim, not the source.** `SortZone.spec.mjs` still leaves the singleton mutated, and that file's own comment already admits the pattern — *"`beforeEach` stubs five methods as OWN properties on the shared singleton; only `onWindowPositionChange` was ever given back. The other four outlived this file."* So it is a **known** leaker that has now cost a second spec a CI-only red. Pinning is correct for this PR and I am not asking you to widen it, but the next spec that reads an ambient `DragCoordinator` config will pay the same tax. Worth a follow-up that restores originals in that teardown instead of assigning constants.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** the body states the AC-6 gap-frame bug you caught *in your own arm before it shipped* — a no-preview frame stored as the candidate's zone erased the last real zone and re-armed a hold the user never left. Written before the code and red on it. Pass.

**Findings:** one, non-blocking, above.
